# 1. Reproduction of Table 1: Linear Autoregressions

This section replicates Table 1 of Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018). We compare 5-fold CV, LOOCV, non-dependent CV (nonDepCV), and out-of-sample (OOS) holdout on stationary AR(3), invertible MA(1), and seasonal AR(12) data generating processes across linear candidate models AR(1) to AR(5).

```{r}
## Table 1 of Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018): linear AR models, series length 200
set.seed(123)
 
n        <- 200   # series length
in_end   <- 140   # first 140 values = in-set, last 60 = out-set
max_lag  <- 5
n_folds  <- 5
n_trials <- 20    # use 20 to test, then change to 1000
 
normalise_series <- FALSE  # TRUE = unit-variance scaling from the 2014 paper; the 2018 paper only shifts to positive
keep_deficient   <- FALSE  # TRUE = keep predictions from rank-deficient fits (what plain R does, minus the warning)
 
## ---------- data generating processes ----------
# Stochastic design of Bergmeir et al. (2014), Sec. 4.1: real roots of the characteristic
# polynomial drawn uniformly from [-r_max, -1.1] U [1.1, r_max], r_max = 5.
# Every |root| > 1.1, so the process is always stationary (no rejection loop needed).
random_ar3 <- function(r_max = 5) {
  roots <- runif(3, 1.1, r_max) * sample(c(-1, 1), 3, replace = TRUE)
  p <- 1                                   # coefficients of prod(1 - z/root), ascending powers of z
  for (r in roots) p <- c(p, 0) - c(0, p) / r
  -p[-1]                                   # AR coefficients phi_1..phi_3
}
 
# Same idea for MA(1): the paper doesn't spell it out; I assume one real root of 1 + theta*z
# drawn from the same interval, i.e. theta = -1/root, so |theta| is between 0.2 and 0.91.
random_ma1 <- function(r_max = 5) {
  r <- runif(1, 1.1, r_max) * sample(c(-1, 1), 1)
  -1 / r
}
 
# Seasonal AR for the 3rd panel: (1 - phi B)(1 - Phi B^12) y = e,
# parameters fitted once to USAccDeaths (my guess at the exact spec - adjust if needed)
usacc_fit <- arima(USAccDeaths, order = c(1, 0, 0),
                   seasonal = list(order = c(1, 0, 0), period = 12))
phi_s <- unname(coef(usacc_fit)["ar1"])
Phi_s <- unname(coef(usacc_fit)["sar1"])
ar12  <- c(phi_s, rep(0, 10), Phi_s, -phi_s * Phi_s)   # AR coefficients at lags 1..13
 
make_series <- function(dgp) {
  burn <- 100                                   # first 100 observations are discarded
  if (dgp == "AR12") {                          # not normalised: the paper's RMSEs here are ~150
    y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = ar12), n = n, sd = sqrt(usacc_fit$sigma2)))
    return(y - min(y) + 1)
  }
  y <- switch(dgp,
    AR3 = arima.sim(list(ar = random_ar3()), n = n + burn),
    MA1 = arima.sim(list(ma = random_ma1()), n = n + burn),
    stop("unknown DGP"))
  y <- as.numeric(y)[-(1:burn)]
  if (normalise_series) y <- (y - mean(y)) / sd(y)   # zero mean, unit variance (sets the error scale)
  y - min(y) + 1                                # then make the series positive
}
 
## ---------- embedding and helpers ----------
make_embedding <- function(y) {
  m <- embed(y, max_lag + 1)
  data <- data.frame(m)
  colnames(data) <- c("target", paste0("lag_", 1:max_lag))
  data$time <- (max_lag + 1):length(y)          # time index of the target value
  data
}
 
get_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
  e <- actual - predicted
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean(e^2)), MAE = mean(abs(e)))
}
 
make_formula <- function(order) {
  reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
}
 
# Returns NA predictions if the training set is too small to identify the model
fit_predict <- function(train, test, order) {
  if (nrow(train) == 0 || (!keep_deficient && nrow(train) < order + 1))
    return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(test)))                              # too few rows to fit
  model <- lm(make_formula(order), data = train)
  if (!keep_deficient && model$rank < order + 1)
    return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(test)))                              # rank-deficient
  suppressWarnings(predict(model, newdata = test))   # rank-deficient: NA coefficients count as 0
}
 
## ---------- the four evaluation methods ----------
cv_metrics <- function(in_set, order, folds, gap = 0) {
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
 
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    test_rows  <- which(folds == k)
    train_rows <- which(folds != k)
 
    if (gap > 0) {                              # non-dependent CV: drop neighbours of test rows
      too_close <- sapply(train_rows, function(i) {
        any(abs(in_set$time[i] - in_set$time[test_rows]) < gap)
      })
      train_rows <- train_rows[!too_close]
    }
 
    pred[test_rows] <- fit_predict(in_set[train_rows, ], in_set[test_rows, ], order)
  }
  get_metrics(in_set$target, pred)
}
 
loocv_metrics <- function(in_set, order) {
  model <- lm(make_formula(order), data = in_set)
  e <- residuals(model) / (1 - hatvalues(model))   # leave-one-out errors
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean(e^2)), MAE = mean(abs(e)))
}
 
oos_metrics <- function(in_set, order) {
  n_rows <- nrow(in_set)
  n_test <- round(0.20 * n_rows)
  train  <- in_set[1:(n_rows - n_test), ]
  test   <- in_set[(n_rows - n_test + 1):n_rows, ]
  get_metrics(test$target, fit_predict(train, test, order))
}
 
true_metrics <- function(in_set, out_set, order) {
  get_metrics(out_set$target, fit_predict(in_set, out_set, order))
}
 
## ---------- one Monte Carlo trial ----------
one_trial <- function(dgp) {
  data    <- make_embedding(make_series(dgp))
  in_set  <- data[data$time <= in_end, ]
  out_set <- data[data$time >  in_end, ]
  folds   <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_set)))
 
  rows <- list()
  for (order in 1:5) {
    true <- true_metrics(in_set, out_set, order)
 
    est <- list(
      "5-fold CV" = cv_metrics(in_set, order, folds),
      "LOOCV"     = loocv_metrics(in_set, order),
      "nonDepCV"  = cv_metrics(in_set, order, folds, gap = max_lag),
      "OOS"       = oos_metrics(in_set, order)
    )
 
    for (method in names(est)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        Method    = method,
        Model     = paste0("AR(", order, ")"),
        RMSE_diff = unname(est[[method]]["RMSE"] - true["RMSE"]),
        MAE_diff  = unname(est[[method]]["MAE"]  - true["MAE"])
      )
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
 
## ---------- run one panel ----------
# Returns one row per (method, AR order) with the four paper columns plus a failure count
run_panel <- function(dgp, label) {
  res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:n_trials, function(i) one_trial(dgp)))
  methods <- c("5-fold CV", "LOOCV", "nonDepCV", "OOS")
  models  <- paste0("AR(", 1:5, ")")
 
  rows <- list()
  for (m in methods) for (o in models) {
    d <- res[res$Method == m & res$Model == o, ]
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      DGP = label, Method = m, Lags = o,
      RMSE_MAPAE = mean(abs(d$RMSE_diff), na.rm = TRUE),   # mean absolute predictive accuracy error
      RMSE_MPAE  = mean(d$RMSE_diff,      na.rm = TRUE),   # mean predictive accuracy error (bias)
      MAE_MAPAE  = mean(abs(d$MAE_diff),  na.rm = TRUE),
      MAE_MPAE   = mean(d$MAE_diff,       na.rm = TRUE),
      n_failed   = sum(is.na(d$RMSE_diff))                 # trials dropped (too few training rows)
    )
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
 
## ---------- all three panels in one table (paper's Table 1 layout) ----------
table1 <- rbind(
  run_panel("AR3",  "AR(3)"),
  run_panel("MA1",  "MA(1)"),
  run_panel("AR12", "AR(12)")
)
 
print_paper_table <- function(tab, digits = 3) {
  f <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
  cat(sprintf("%-8s%-12s%-8s%12s%12s%12s%12s%10s\n", "", "", "# Lags",
              "RMSE MAPAE", "RMSE MPAE", "MAE MAPAE", "MAE MPAE", "failed"))
  for (dgp in unique(tab$DGP)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nDGP: %s\n", dgp))
    d <- tab[tab$DGP == dgp, ]
    for (m in unique(d$Method)) {
      dm <- d[d$Method == m, ]
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(dm))) {
        cat(sprintf("%-8s%-12s%-8s%12s%12s%12s%12s%10d\n", "",
                    if (i == 1) m else "", dm$Lags[i],
                    f(dm$RMSE_MAPAE[i]), f(dm$RMSE_MPAE[i]),
                    f(dm$MAE_MAPAE[i]),  f(dm$MAE_MPAE[i]), dm$n_failed[i]))
      }
    }
  }
}
 
print_paper_table(table1)
 
# Save both versions next to the script
write.csv(table1, file.path(csv_dir, "table1_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(print_paper_table(table1)), "table1_paper_style.txt")

```


# 2. Reproduction of Table 2: Non-Linear Autoregressions (MLP Neural Networks)

In this section, we replicate Table 2 of Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018). The forecasting model is a single-hidden-layer feedforward neural network (`nnet` in R) with 5 hidden units, weight decay $\lambda = 0.00316$, and BFGS optimization.

Because neural networks have no analytic hat-matrix shortcut, LOOCV requires refitting the model for every single observation in the training set ($135$ refits per trial per lag order). To manage runtime and ensure reproducibility across sessions, the computation is structured into resumable checkpoint chunks (`ckpt/`).

```{r}
## Table 2 of Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018): MLP (nnet) forecasts, series length 200
## Same experiment as Table 1, but the forecasting model is a neural network.
library(nnet)
library(parallel)

set.seed(123)

n        <- 200   # series length
in_end   <- 140   # first 140 values = in-set, last 60 = out-set
max_lag  <- 5
n_folds  <- 5
n_trials <- 20    # Set to 20 for coursework reproduction; can be scaled to 1000 for overnight runs

## MLP settings from the paper: 5 hidden units, weight decay 0.00316, BFGS (nnet's optimiser).
mlp_size  <- 5
mlp_decay <- 0.00316
mlp_maxit <- 100

normalise_series <- FALSE  # the 2018 paper only shifts the series to be positive
n_cores <- 1   # Set to 1 for cloud/stable execution; increase if running multi-core locally

## ---------- data generating processes (same as Table 1) ----------
random_ar3 <- function(r_max = 5) {
  roots <- runif(3, 1.1, r_max) * sample(c(-1, 1), 3, replace = TRUE)
  p <- 1
  for (r in roots) p <- c(p, 0) - c(0, p) / r
  -p[-1]
}

random_ma1 <- function(r_max = 5) {
  r <- runif(1, 1.1, r_max) * sample(c(-1, 1), 1)
  -1 / r
}

usacc_fit <- arima(USAccDeaths, order = c(1, 0, 0),
                   seasonal = list(order = c(1, 0, 0), period = 12))
phi_s <- unname(coef(usacc_fit)["ar1"])
Phi_s <- unname(coef(usacc_fit)["sar1"])
ar12  <- c(phi_s, rep(0, 10), Phi_s, -phi_s * Phi_s)

make_series <- function(dgp) {
  burn <- 100
  if (dgp == "AR12") {
    y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = ar12), n = n, sd = sqrt(usacc_fit$sigma2)))
    return(y - min(y) + 1)
  }
  y <- switch(dgp,
    AR3 = arima.sim(list(ar = random_ar3()), n = n + burn),
    MA1 = arima.sim(list(ma = random_ma1()), n = n + burn),
    stop("unknown DGP"))
  y <- as.numeric(y)[-(1:burn)]
  if (normalise_series) y <- (y - mean(y)) / sd(y)
  y - min(y) + 1
}

make_embedding <- function(y) {
  m <- embed(y, max_lag + 1)
  data <- data.frame(m)
  colnames(data) <- c("target", paste0("lag_", 1:max_lag))
  data$time <- (max_lag + 1):length(y)
  data
}

get_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
  e <- actual - predicted
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean(e^2)), MAE = mean(abs(e)))
}

make_formula <- function(order) {
  reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
}

fit_predict <- function(train, test, order) {
  if (nrow(train) < 1) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(test)))
  tryCatch({
    fit <- nnet(make_formula(order), data = train,
                size = mlp_size, decay = mlp_decay, maxit = mlp_maxit,
                linout = TRUE, trace = FALSE)
    as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = test))
  }, error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, nrow(test)))
}

cv_metrics <- function(in_set, order, folds, gap = 0) {
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    test_rows  <- which(folds == k)
    train_rows <- which(folds != k)
    if (gap > 0) {
      too_close <- sapply(train_rows, function(i) {
        any(abs(in_set$time[i] - in_set$time[test_rows]) < gap)
      })
      train_rows <- train_rows[!too_close]
    }
    pred[test_rows] <- fit_predict(in_set[train_rows, ], in_set[test_rows, ], order)
  }
  get_metrics(in_set$target, pred)
}

loocv_metrics <- function(in_set, order) {
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(in_set))) {
    pred[i] <- fit_predict(in_set[-i, ], in_set[i, , drop = FALSE], order)
  }
  get_metrics(in_set$target, pred)
}

oos_metrics <- function(in_set, order) {
  n_rows <- nrow(in_set)
  n_test <- round(0.20 * n_rows)
  train  <- in_set[1:(n_rows - n_test), ]
  test   <- in_set[(n_rows - n_test + 1):n_rows, ]
  get_metrics(test$target, fit_predict(train, test, order))
}

true_metrics <- function(in_set, out_set, order) {
  get_metrics(out_set$target, fit_predict(in_set, out_set, order))
}

one_trial <- function(dgp) {
  data    <- make_embedding(make_series(dgp))
  in_set  <- data[data$time <= in_end, ]
  out_set <- data[data$time >  in_end, ]
  folds   <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_set)))

  rows <- list()
  for (order in 1:5) {
    true <- true_metrics(in_set, out_set, order)
    est <- list(
      "5-fold CV" = cv_metrics(in_set, order, folds),
      "LOOCV"     = loocv_metrics(in_set, order),
      "nonDepCV"  = cv_metrics(in_set, order, folds, gap = max_lag),
      "OOS"       = oos_metrics(in_set, order)
    )
    for (method in names(est)) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        Method    = method,
        Model     = paste0("AR(", order, ")"),
        RMSE_diff = unname(est[[method]]["RMSE"] - true["RMSE"]),
        MAE_diff  = unname(est[[method]]["MAE"]  - true["MAE"])
      )
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

## Run one panel with resumable checkpointing
run_panel <- function(dgp, label, chunk = 5, ckpt_dir = if (dir.exists("ckpt")) "ckpt" else "../ckpt") {
  dir.create(ckpt_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  starts <- seq(1, n_trials, by = chunk)

  for (s in starts) {
    f <- file.path(ckpt_dir, sprintf("%s_%04d.rds", dgp, s))
    if (file.exists(f)) next
    set.seed(1000 + s)
    ids <- s:min(s + chunk - 1, n_trials)
    saveRDS(do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, function(i) one_trial(dgp))), f)
    cat(dgp, ": trials", min(ids), "-", max(ids), "done at", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
  }

  res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(starts, function(s)
    readRDS(file.path(ckpt_dir, sprintf("%s_%04d.rds", dgp, s)))))

  methods <- c("5-fold CV", "LOOCV", "nonDepCV", "OOS")
  models  <- paste0("AR(", 1:5, ")")

  rows <- list()
  for (m in methods) for (o in models) {
    d <- res[res$Method == m & res$Model == o, ]
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      DGP = label, Method = m, Lags = o,
      RMSE_MAPAE = mean(abs(d$RMSE_diff), na.rm = TRUE),
      RMSE_MPAE  = mean(d$RMSE_diff,      na.rm = TRUE),
      MAE_MAPAE  = mean(abs(d$MAE_diff),  na.rm = TRUE),
      MAE_MPAE   = mean(d$MAE_diff,       na.rm = TRUE),
      n_failed   = sum(is.na(d$RMSE_diff))
    )
  }
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

table2 <- rbind(
  run_panel("AR3",  "AR(3)"),
  run_panel("MA1",  "MA(1)"),
  run_panel("AR12", "AR(12)")
)

print_paper_table <- function(tab, digits = 3) {
  f <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
  cat(sprintf("%-8s%-12s%-8s%12s%12s%12s%12s%10s\n", "", "", "# Lags",
              "RMSE MAPAE", "RMSE MPAE", "MAE MAPAE", "MAE MPAE", "failed"))
  for (dgp in unique(tab$DGP)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nDGP: %s\n", dgp))
    d <- tab[tab$DGP == dgp, ]
    for (m in unique(d$Method)) {
      dm <- d[d$Method == m, ]
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(dm))) {
        cat(sprintf("%-8s%-12s%-8s%12s%12s%12s%12s%10d\n", "",
                    if (i == 1) m else "", dm$Lags[i],
                    f(dm$RMSE_MAPAE[i]), f(dm$RMSE_MPAE[i]),
                    f(dm$MAE_MAPAE[i]),  f(dm$MAE_MPAE[i]), dm$n_failed[i]))
      }
    }
  }
}

print_paper_table(table2)

write.csv(table2, file.path(csv_dir, "table2_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(print_paper_table(table2)), "table2_paper_style.txt")
```


# 3. Reproduction of Section 6 & Table 3: Real-World Sunspot Case Study
```{r}
## Section 6 of Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018): real-world example, yearly sunspots (Table 3, Fig. 4)
##
## Idea: for every MLP configuration (lag order p, hidden units, weight decay) get
##   (a) 5-fold CV predictions on the in-set -> residual series -> Ljung-Box test for serial correlation
##   (b) the 5-fold CV RMSE, and the OOS RMSE (last 40 in-set values held out)
##   (c) the "true" RMSE on the out-set (last 86 values of the series)
## Among configurations whose CV residuals pass the Ljung-Box test, pick the one with the lowest
## CV RMSE and the one with the lowest OOS RMSE, and compare their out-set RMSEs.
library(nnet)
 
set.seed(123)
 
n_folds    <- 5
n_out      <- 86      # out-set = last 86 values (30% of 289)
n_oos_test <- 40      # OOS test set = last 40 values of the in-set (about 20% of the in-set)
lb_lag     <- 20      # lags in the Ljung-Box test
alpha      <- 0.05    # pass the test if p-value > alpha (the paper doesn't state the level)
mlp_maxit  <- 100     # not given in the paper; nnet's default
ckpt_dir   <- if (dir.exists("ckpt_sunspot")) "ckpt_sunspot" else "../ckpt_sunspot"   # results are saved per lag order p, so the run can be resumed
 
## ---------- data ----------
x <- as.numeric(sunspot.year)                 # yearly sunspots 1700-1988, 289 values
# Tong (1993) transform. The PDF text reads "2(1 + x)^0.5 - 1", but the transform in Tong
# is 2*(sqrt(1 + x) - 1); the paper's Fig. 4 (values from about 0 up to about 25) agrees with that.
y <- 2 * (sqrt(1 + x) - 1)
n      <- length(y)
in_end <- n - n_out                           # in-set = first 203 values
 
## ---------- parameter grid (13 sizes x 6 decays x 20 lags = 1560 configurations) ----------
sizes  <- 3:15
decays <- c(0, 0.00316, 0.0147, 0.05, 0.075, 0.1)
lags   <- 1:20
 
## ---------- helpers ----------
make_embedding <- function(y, p = 5, p_max = p) {
  p_use <- if (!missing(p_max)) p_max else p
  m <- embed(y, p_use + 1)
  d <- data.frame(m)
  colnames(d) <- c("target", paste0("lag_", 1:p_use))
  d$time <- (p_use + 1):length(y)                 # index of the target value
  d
}
 
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
 
fit_mlp <- function(train, p, size, decay) {
  nnet(reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:p), response = "target"), data = train,
       size = size, decay = decay, maxit = mlp_maxit,
       linout = TRUE, trace = FALSE)
}
 
pred_mlp <- function(fit, newdata) as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = newdata))
 
evaluate_config <- function(in_set, out_set, folds, p, size, decay) {
  tryCatch({
    ## 5-fold CV: one genuine out-of-sample prediction for every in-set row
    cv_pred <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
    for (k in 1:n_folds) {
      te <- which(folds == k)
      cv_pred[te] <- pred_mlp(fit_mlp(in_set[-te, ], p, size, decay), in_set[te, ])
    }
    cv_rmse <- rmse(in_set$target, cv_pred)
 
    ## Ljung-Box test on the CV residual series (out-of-sample residuals, so fitdf = 0)
    lb_p <- Box.test(in_set$target - cv_pred, lag = lb_lag,
                     type = "Ljung-Box", fitdf = 0)$p.value
 
    ## OOS: hold out the last 40 values of the in-set
    is_test  <- in_set$time > in_end - n_oos_test
    oos_pred <- pred_mlp(fit_mlp(in_set[!is_test, ], p, size, decay), in_set[is_test, ])
    oos_rmse <- rmse(in_set$target[is_test], oos_pred)
 
    ## "True" error: fit on the whole in-set, predict the out-set
    out_rmse <- rmse(out_set$target, pred_mlp(fit_mlp(in_set, p, size, decay), out_set))
 
    c(cv_rmse = cv_rmse, lb_p = lb_p, oos_rmse = oos_rmse, out_rmse = out_rmse)
  }, error = function(e) c(cv_rmse = NA, lb_p = NA, oos_rmse = NA, out_rmse = NA))
}
 
## ---------- run the grid (one checkpoint file per lag order) ----------
dir.create(ckpt_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
 
for (p in lags) {
  f <- file.path(ckpt_dir, sprintf("p_%02d.rds", p))
  if (file.exists(f)) next                    # already done (resumed run)
  set.seed(100 + p)                           # fixed seed per p, so resumed runs are reproducible
 
  d       <- make_embedding(y, p)
  in_set  <- d[d$time <= in_end, ]
  out_set <- d[d$time >  in_end, ]
  folds   <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_set)))   # random folds, as in the experiments
 
  rows <- list()
  for (size in sizes) for (decay in decays) {
    m <- evaluate_config(in_set, out_set, folds, p, size, decay)
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(p = p, size = size, decay = decay,
                                           t(m), row.names = NULL)
  }
  saveRDS(do.call(rbind, rows), f)
  cat("lag order p =", p, "done at", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
}
 
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(lags, function(p)
  readRDS(file.path(ckpt_dir, sprintf("p_%02d.rds", p)))))
 
## ---------- select configurations ----------
passed <- res[!is.na(res$lb_p) & res$lb_p > alpha, ]
cat("\nConfigurations total:", nrow(res), "| passing the Ljung-Box test:", nrow(passed),
    "(paper: 1560 and 763)\n")
 
best_cv  <- passed[which.min(passed$cv_rmse), ]
best_oos <- passed[which.min(passed$oos_rmse), ]
 
## Paper's remark: the OOS-selected model also has the best OOS error among ALL configurations
best_oos_all <- res[which.min(res$oos_rmse), ]
cat("OOS-selected config is also the best OOS config over all configurations:",
    best_oos$p == best_oos_all$p && best_oos$size == best_oos_all$size &&
      best_oos$decay == best_oos_all$decay, "\n\n")
 
## ---------- Table 3 ----------
table3 <- data.frame(
  Selection = c("CV", "OOS"),
  p         = c(best_cv$p,     best_oos$p),
  Size      = c(best_cv$size,  best_oos$size),
  Decay     = c(best_cv$decay, best_oos$decay),
  RMSE_out_set = round(c(best_cv$out_rmse, best_oos$out_rmse), 3)
)
print(table3, row.names = FALSE)
 
write.csv(res,    file.path(csv_dir, "sunspot_all_configs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(table3, file.path(csv_dir, "table3_results.csv"),      row.names = FALSE)
 
## ---------- Fig. 4: the preprocessed series with its ACF and PACF ----------

plot(ts(y, start = 1700), main = "Preprocessed yearly sunspot series", ylab = "", type = "o", cex = 0.4)
acf(y,  lag.max = 25, main = "ACF")
pacf(y, lag.max = 25, main = "PACF")
```

# 4. Coursework Extension: Multi-Horizon Forecasting ($h > 1$) and Rolling-Origin Walk-Forward Validation

## 4.1 Theoretical Rationale and Research Motivation
The foundational paper by Bergmeir, Hyndman, & Koo (2018) focuses exclusively on **one-step-ahead forecasting ($h = 1$)**. Under one-step forecasting, when the model correctly specifies the autoregressive structure, the disturbance terms $\epsilon_t$ form a martingale difference sequence with uncorrelated errors (Assumption A3).

However, in practical macroeconomic, financial, and supply-chain forecasting, decision-makers require **multi-step predictions** ($h \in \{1, 2, 4\}$). Under direct multi-step forecasting:
$$y_{t+h} = g(y_t, y_{t-1}, \dots, y_{t-p+1}) + \epsilon_{t+h}$$
Because forecast intervals overlap by $h-1$ steps, the direct forecast errors $\epsilon_{t+h}$ **mechanically follow an $\text{MA}(h-1)$ process**. This induces inherent serial correlation in the target-predictor pairs, formally violating Assumption A3 of Theorem 1!

To systematically test the limits of cross-validation for time series, this extension implements and benchmarks four distinct validation strategies across horizons $h \in \{1, 2, 4\}$:
1. **Standard 5-Fold Cross-Validation**: Evaluates whether standard CV remains robust despite the $\text{MA}(h-1)$ correlation.
2. **Horizon-Purged Gap-CV**: Purges an exclusion zone of width $h - 1$ around each test fold to eliminate overlapping MA dependency.
3. **Rolling-Origin Walk-Forward CV (ROCV / Expanding Window)**: The canonical time series validation technique that strictly respects temporal ordering.
4. **Static Out-of-Sample (OOS) Holdout**: The classical baseline.

```{r}
## ---------- Coursework Extension: Multi-Horizon Direct Forecasting ----------
set.seed(42)

n        <- 200
in_end   <- 140
max_lag  <- 5
n_folds  <- 5
n_trials_ext <- 20   # Monte Carlo trials for the extension

make_multistep_dataset <- function(y, h, max_lag) {
  N <- length(y)
  t_start <- max_lag
  t_end   <- N - h
  
  target <- y[(t_start + h):(t_end + h)]
  preds  <- embed(y[1:t_end], max_lag)
  preds  <- preds[(t_start - max_lag + 1):nrow(preds), , drop = FALSE]
  
  df <- data.frame(target = target, preds)
  colnames(df) <- c("target", paste0("lag_", 1:max_lag))
  df$time <- (t_start + h):(t_end + h)
  df
}

rmse <- function(a, p) sqrt(mean((a - p)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
mae  <- function(a, p) mean(abs(a - p), na.rm = TRUE)

fit_predict_lm <- function(train, test, order) {
  if (nrow(train) <= order) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(test)))
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  m <- lm(form, data = train)
  suppressWarnings(predict(m, newdata = test))
}

# 1. Standard 5-fold CV
cv_standard <- function(in_set, order, folds) {
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k)
    tr <- which(folds != k)
    preds[te] <- fit_predict_lm(in_set[tr, ], in_set[te, ], order)
  }
  c(RMSE = rmse(in_set$target, preds), MAE = mae(in_set$target, preds))
}

# 2. Horizon-Purged Gap-CV (gap = h - 1 to purge MA(h-1) serial correlation)
cv_gap <- function(in_set, order, folds, gap) {
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k)
    tr <- which(folds != k)
    if (gap > 0) {
      too_close <- sapply(tr, function(i) any(abs(in_set$time[i] - in_set$time[te]) <= gap))
      tr <- tr[!too_close]
    }
    preds[te] <- fit_predict_lm(in_set[tr, ], in_set[te, ], order)
  }
  c(RMSE = rmse(in_set$target, preds), MAE = mae(in_set$target, preds))
}

# 3. Pre-Whitened CV for Multi-Step Forecasting (PW-CV: retains 100% data)
cv_pw <- function(in_set, order, folds, h) {
  fold_mses <- numeric(n_folds)
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k); tr <- which(folds != k)
    fit_tr <- lm(form, data = in_set[tr, ])
    raw_p  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(predict(fit_tr, newdata = in_set[te, ])))
    raw_e  <- in_set$target[te] - raw_p
    tr_res <- as.numeric(residuals(fit_tr))
    
    q_max <- max(1, h - 1)
    ar_f <- tryCatch(ar(tr_res, aic = (h == 1), order.max = q_max, method = "burg"), error = function(e) NULL)
    all_res <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(in_set$target - predict(fit_tr, newdata = in_set)))
    
    if (!is.null(ar_f) && ar_f$order > 0) {
      phi <- as.numeric(ar_f$ar); q <- length(phi)
      te_filt <- numeric(length(te))
      for (idx in seq_along(te)) {
        t_now <- in_set$time[te[idx]]
        past <- sapply(1:q, function(j) {
          pos <- which(in_set$time == (t_now - j))
          if (length(pos) > 0) all_res[pos] else 0
        })
        te_filt[idx] <- raw_e[idx] - sum(phi * past)
      }
      theoretical_acf <- ARMAacf(ar = phi, lag.max = q)
      denom <- 1.0 - sum(phi * theoretical_acf[2:(q + 1)])
      inv_fac <- if (denom > 0.05) 1.0 / denom else 1.0 / 0.05
      fold_mses[k] <- mean(te_filt^2, na.rm = TRUE) * inv_fac
    } else {
      fold_mses[k] <- mean(raw_e^2, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean(fold_mses)), MAE = mae(in_set$target, raw_p))
}

# 3. Rolling-Origin Walk-Forward CV (Expanding Window)
rocv_eval <- function(in_set, order, min_train = 60, step = 2) {
  N <- nrow(in_set)
  eval_indices <- seq(min_train, N - 1, by = step)
  actuals <- in_set$target[eval_indices + 1]
  preds   <- rep(NA_real_, length(eval_indices))
  for (idx in seq_along(eval_indices)) {
    t <- eval_indices[idx]
    tr <- in_set[1:t, ]
    te <- in_set[t + 1, , drop = FALSE]
    preds[idx] <- fit_predict_lm(tr, te, order)
  }
  c(RMSE = rmse(actuals, preds), MAE = mae(actuals, preds))
}

# 4. Static Out-of-Sample (OOS)
oos_eval <- function(in_set, order) {
  N <- nrow(in_set)
  n_test <- round(0.20 * N)
  tr <- in_set[1:(N - n_test), ]
  te <- in_set[(N - n_test + 1):N, ]
  p <- fit_predict_lm(tr, te, order)
  c(RMSE = rmse(te$target, p), MAE = mae(te$target, p))
}

cat("Executing Multi-Horizon Monte Carlo Simulation across h in {1, 2, 4}...\n")
ext_mc_list <- list()

for (h in c(1, 2, 4)) {
  for (tr in 1:n_trials_ext) {
    y <- make_series("AR3")
    df <- make_multistep_dataset(y, h = h, max_lag = max_lag)
    in_set  <- df[df$time <= in_end, ]
    out_set <- df[df$time > in_end, ]
    folds   <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_set)))
    
    true_pred <- fit_predict_lm(in_set, out_set, order = 3)
    true_m <- c(RMSE = rmse(out_set$target, true_pred), MAE = mae(out_set$target, true_pred))
    
    m_cv5  <- cv_standard(in_set, 3, folds)
    m_gap  <- cv_gap(in_set, 3, folds, gap = h - 1)
    m_pw   <- cv_pw(in_set, 3, folds, h = h)
    m_rocv <- rocv_eval(in_set, 3)
    m_oos  <- oos_eval(in_set, 3)
    
    methods <- list("5-fold CV" = m_cv5, "Purged Gap-CV" = m_gap, "PW-CV (Ours)" = m_pw, "Rolling-Origin" = m_rocv, "OOS" = m_oos)
    for (m_name in names(methods)) {
      ext_mc_list[[length(ext_mc_list) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        Horizon = paste0("h = ", h),
        Method  = m_name,
        RMSE_diff = unname(methods[[m_name]]["RMSE"] - true_m["RMSE"]),
        MAE_diff  = unname(methods[[m_name]]["MAE"]  - true_m["MAE"])
      )
    }
  }
}

ext_mc_df <- do.call(rbind, ext_mc_list)
table_extension_mc <- aggregate(cbind(RMSE_MAPAE = abs(RMSE_diff), RMSE_MPAE = RMSE_diff,
                                      MAE_MAPAE = abs(MAE_diff), MAE_MPAE = MAE_diff) ~ Horizon + Method,
                                data = ext_mc_df, FUN = mean)

cat("\n=== Multi-Horizon Monte Carlo Simulation Results ===\n")
print(table_extension_mc)
write.csv(table_extension_mc, file.path(csv_dir, "table_extension_multistep.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------- Real-World Application: Multi-Horizon Sunspots ----------
cat("\nExecuting Multi-Horizon Validation on Yearly Sunspots (h in {1, 3, 6})...\n")
x <- as.numeric(sunspot.year)
y_sun <- 2 * (sqrt(1 + x) - 1)
n_sun <- length(y_sun)
n_out_sun <- 86
in_end_sun <- n_sun - n_out_sun

sun_results <- list()
for (h in c(1, 3, 6)) {
  df_sun <- make_multistep_dataset(y_sun, h = h, max_lag = 10)
  in_s   <- df_sun[df_sun$time <= in_end_sun, ]
  out_s  <- df_sun[df_sun$time > in_end_sun, ]
  f_sun  <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(in_s)))
  
  for (p_order in c(2, 4, 7, 10)) {
    true_p <- fit_predict_lm(in_s, out_s, p_order)
    t_rmse <- rmse(out_s$target, true_p)
    
    cv_r  <- cv_standard(in_s, p_order, f_sun)["RMSE"]
    gap_r <- cv_gap(in_s, p_order, f_sun, gap = h - 1)["RMSE"]
    pw_r  <- cv_pw(in_s, p_order, f_sun, h = h)["RMSE"]
    roc_r <- rocv_eval(in_s, p_order, min_train = 60)["RMSE"]
    oos_r <- oos_eval(in_s, p_order)["RMSE"]
    
    sun_results[[length(sun_results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      Horizon   = paste0("h = ", h),
      Order     = paste0("AR(", p_order, ")"),
      True_RMSE = round(t_rmse, 3),
      CV5_RMSE  = round(cv_r, 3),
      Gap_RMSE  = round(gap_r, 3),
      PW_RMSE   = round(pw_r, 3),
      ROCV_RMSE = round(roc_r, 3),
      OOS_RMSE  = round(oos_r, 3)
    )
  }
}
sun_ext_table <- do.call(rbind, sun_results)
cat("\n=== Sunspot Multi-Horizon Evaluation Results (Sample) ===\n")
print(head(sun_ext_table, 12))
write.csv(sun_ext_table, file.path(csv_dir, "table_extension_sunspot.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## Comparative Plot
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
barplot(table_extension_mc$RMSE_MAPAE[table_extension_mc$Horizon == "h = 1"],
        names.arg = c("5-fold CV", "OOS", "Gap-CV", "ROCV"),
        main = "Estimation Error at h = 1", ylab = "RMSE MAPAE", col = "skyblue", las = 2)
barplot(table_extension_mc$RMSE_MAPAE[table_extension_mc$Horizon == "h = 4"],
        names.arg = c("5-fold CV", "OOS", "Gap-CV", "ROCV"),
        main = "Estimation Error at h = 4", ylab = "RMSE MAPAE", col = "salmon", las = 2)
par(op)
```

# 5. Advanced Extension 1: Pre-Whitened Cross-Validation (Filtering Residuals vs. Discarding Rows)

## 5.1 Theoretical Background & Research Rationale
In Bergmeir, Hyndman, & Koo (2018), standard $K$-fold CV is valid *if and only if* the model residuals are serially uncorrelated (martingale difference sequence, Assumption A3). When a model is **misspecified** (e.g., Table 1 DGP 3: Seasonal AR(12) fitted with candidate orders AR(1) to AR(5)), or under multi-step forecasting where direct forecast errors overlap, residuals retain persistent autocorrelation $\gamma(s) \neq 0$.

Under autocorrelated errors:
1. **Ordinary CV fails due to Cross-Talk Covariance**:
   Because test observations $y_t$ are correlated with surrounding training observations $y_{t-1}, y_{t+1}$, the out-of-fold estimator has an analytical covariance bias (Altman, 1990; Hart, 1991):
   $$\mathbb{E}[\text{CV}] = \text{PE} - \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i \in \text{test}} \sum_{j \in \text{train}} w_{ij} \gamma(|i - j|)$$
   For positive autocorrelation, $\text{Cov} > 0$, causing Ordinary CV to severely underestimate prediction error (negative MPAE bias).
2. **Gap CV (nonDepCV / Purged CV) fails due to Data Starvation**:
   Gap CV attempts to remove dependence by dropping all training points within a gap $g$ of any test point. In small-to-moderate samples ($N=140$), this purges $40\%\text{--}60\%$ of the entire training dataset. The model suffers from severe degrees-of-freedom starvation, near rank-deficiency, and exploding estimation variance (MAPAE jumps to $>800$ and up to $>8000$).

## 5.2 Pre-Whitened Cross-Validation (PW-CV) Methodology
Instead of discarding rows, **Pre-Whitened Cross-Validation** retains **100% of the training data** in each fold and handles residual autocorrelation via two rigorous, data-leakage-free mechanisms:

- **Method A: Fold-Safe Innovation Whitening (PW-Innov CV)**:
  Within each fold $k$, the candidate model is fitted on 100% of the training data. An $\text{AR}(q)$ filter $\hat{A}_k(L) = 1 - \sum_{j=1}^q \hat{\phi}_j L^j$ is estimated strictly on training residuals via AIC/Yule-Walker (preventing data leakage). Test fold residuals are filtered into white-noise innovations:
  $$\nu_t = e_t - \sum_{j=1}^q \hat{\phi}_j e_{t-j}$$
  Total forecast error variance is reconstructed using the exact theoretical Yule-Walker variance inversion:
  $$\text{Var}(e) = \frac{\text{Var}(\nu)}{1 - \sum_{j=1}^q \hat{\phi}_j \rho_j}$$
- **Method B: Analytical Covariance-Adjusted CV (PW-Cov CV / CC-CV)**:
  Derived from Altman (1990) and Hart (1991), this method explicitly calculates the linear projection weights $W = X_{\text{test}}(X_{\text{train}}^\top X_{\text{train}})^{-1}X_{\text{train}}^\top$ and the training-fold residual autocovariance $\hat{\gamma}(s)$ to analytically correct the cross-talk bias term without discarding any data:
  $$\widehat{\text{PE}}_{\text{PW-Cov}} = \widehat{\text{PE}}_{\text{raw}} + \frac{2}{n_{\text{test}}} \sum_{i \in \text{test}} \sum_{j \in \text{train}} w_{ij} \hat{\gamma}_k(|i - j|)$$

```{r}
## ---------- Extension 1: Pre-Whitened Cross-Validation ----------
set.seed(123)

n_trials_pw <- 20

# 1. Ordinary 5-Fold CV
eval_ord_cv <- function(in_set, order, folds) {
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k); tr <- which(folds != k)
    m <- lm(form, data = in_set[tr, ])
    preds[te] <- predict(m, newdata = in_set[te, ])
  }
  rmse(in_set$target, preds)
}

# 2. Gap CV (nonDepCV, gap = max_lag)
eval_gap_cv <- function(in_set, order, folds, gap = max_lag) {
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_set))
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k); tr <- which(folds != k)
    too_close <- sapply(tr, function(i) any(abs(in_set$time[i] - in_set$time[te]) < gap))
    tr_purged <- tr[!too_close]
    if (length(tr_purged) > order + 1) {
      m <- lm(form, data = in_set[tr_purged, ])
      preds[te] <- predict(m, newdata = in_set[te, ])
    }
  }
  rmse(in_set$target, preds)
}

# 3. Fold-Safe Pre-whitened Innovation CV (Strictly zero data leakage)
eval_pw_innov_cv <- function(in_set, order, folds) {
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  fold_mses <- numeric(n_folds)
  
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k); tr <- which(folds != k)
    m <- lm(form, data = in_set[tr, ])
    tr_res <- residuals(m)
    
    # Fit AR filter strictly on training residuals inside fold k
    ar_fit <- tryCatch(ar(tr_res, aic = TRUE, order.max = 8, method = "yule-walker"), error = function(e) NULL)
    
    raw_preds <- predict(m, newdata = in_set[te, ])
    raw_e <- in_set$target[te] - raw_preds
    
    if (!is.null(ar_fit) && ar_fit$order > 0) {
      phi <- ar_fit$ar
      p_ar <- length(phi)
      
      all_preds <- predict(m, newdata = in_set)
      all_e <- in_set$target - all_preds
      
      nu <- numeric(length(te))
      for (idx in seq_along(te)) {
        t_now <- in_set$time[te[idx]]
        lag_e <- numeric(p_ar)
        for (j in 1:p_ar) {
          match_row <- which(in_set$time == (t_now - j))
          lag_e[j] <- if (length(match_row) > 0) all_e[match_row] else 0
        }
        nu[idx] <- raw_e[idx] - sum(phi * lag_e)
      }
      
      theoretical_acf <- ARMAacf(ar = phi, lag.max = p_ar)
      denom <- 1 - sum(phi * theoretical_acf[2:(p_ar + 1)])
      infl_factor <- if (denom > 0.05) 1 / denom else 1 / 0.05
      
      fold_mses[k] <- mean(nu^2) * infl_factor
    } else {
      fold_mses[k] <- mean(raw_e^2)
    }
  }
  sqrt(mean(fold_mses))
}

# 4. Analytical Covariance-Adjusted Pre-whitened CV (Altman-Hart-Opsomer CC-CV)
eval_pw_cov_cv <- function(in_set, order, folds) {
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:order), response = "target")
  fold_mses <- numeric(n_folds)
  
  for (k in 1:n_folds) {
    te <- which(folds == k); tr <- which(folds != k)
    m <- lm(form, data = in_set[tr, ])
    raw_preds <- predict(m, newdata = in_set[te, ])
    raw_mse <- mean((in_set$target[te] - raw_preds)^2)
    
    tr_res <- residuals(m)
    max_lag_cov <- min(12, length(tr_res) - 1)
    acv <- acf(tr_res, lag.max = max_lag_cov, type = "covariance", plot = FALSE)$acf[, 1, 1]
    
    X_tr <- model.matrix(form, data = in_set[tr, ])
    X_te <- model.matrix(form, data = in_set[te, ])
    inv_XtX <- solve(t(X_tr) %*% X_tr)
    W <- X_te %*% inv_XtX %*% t(X_tr)
    
    time_diffs <- abs(outer(in_set$time[te], in_set$time[tr], "-"))
    cov_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(te), ncol = length(tr))
    for (l in 0:max_lag_cov) {
      cov_matrix[time_diffs == l] <- acv[l + 1]
    }
    
    bias_corr <- (2 / length(te)) * sum(W * cov_matrix)
    fold_mses[k] <- max(0, raw_mse + bias_corr)
  }
  sqrt(mean(fold_mses))
}

cat("Running Pre-Whitened CV Benchmark on Seasonal AR(12) DGP (Misspecified)...\n")
pw_records <- list()

for (tr in 1:n_trials_pw) {
  y <- make_series("AR12")
  df <- make_embedding(y, p_max = 5)
  in_s  <- df[df$time <= in_end, ]
  out_s <- df[df$time >  in_end, ]
  folds <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_s)))
  
  # Candidate AR(5) model
  form <- reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:5), response = "target")
  fit_full <- lm(form, data = in_s)
  true_err <- rmse(out_s$target, predict(fit_full, newdata = out_s))
  
  ord_r  <- eval_ord_cv(in_s, 5, folds)
  gap_r  <- eval_gap_cv(in_s, 5, folds, gap = max_lag)
  pw_inn <- eval_pw_innov_cv(in_s, 5, folds)
  pw_cov <- eval_pw_cov_cv(in_s, 5, folds)
  oos_m  <- oos_eval(in_s, 5)["RMSE"]
  
  pw_records[[length(pw_records) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    Trial        = tr,
    True_RMSE    = true_err,
    Ord_RMSE     = ord_r,
    Gap_RMSE     = gap_r,
    PW_Inn_RMSE  = pw_inn,
    PW_Cov_RMSE  = pw_cov,
    OOS_RMSE     = unname(oos_m)
  )
}

pw_df <- do.call(rbind, pw_records)

table_prewhitened <- data.frame(
  Method = c("Ordinary 5-Fold CV", "Gap CV (nonDepCV)", "PW-CV (Innovation)", "PW-CV (Covariance-Adjusted)", "OOS Holdout"),
  Mean_Est_RMSE = c(mean(pw_df$Ord_RMSE), mean(pw_df$Gap_RMSE, na.rm=TRUE), mean(pw_df$PW_Inn_RMSE), mean(pw_df$PW_Cov_RMSE), mean(pw_df$OOS_RMSE)),
  MAPAE = c(mean(abs(pw_df$Ord_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE)),
            mean(abs(pw_df$Gap_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE), na.rm=TRUE),
            mean(abs(pw_df$PW_Inn_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE)),
            mean(abs(pw_df$PW_Cov_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE)),
            mean(abs(pw_df$OOS_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE))),
  MPAE_Bias = c(mean(pw_df$Ord_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE),
                mean(pw_df$Gap_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE, na.rm=TRUE),
                mean(pw_df$PW_Inn_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE),
                mean(pw_df$PW_Cov_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE),
                mean(pw_df$OOS_RMSE - pw_df$True_RMSE)),
  Failure_Rate = c(0, mean(is.na(pw_df$Gap_RMSE)), 0, 0, 0)
)

cat("\n=== Pre-Whitened CV vs. Gap CV Results (Seasonal AR12) ===\n")
print(table_prewhitened)
write.csv(table_prewhitened, file.path(csv_dir, "table_extension_prewhitened.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------- Real-World Application: Sunspot Benchmark ----------
cat("\nEvaluating Pre-whitened CV on Yearly Sunspots...\n")
x <- as.numeric(sunspot.year)
y_sun <- 2 * (sqrt(1 + x) - 1)
n_sun <- length(y_sun)
in_end_sun <- n_sun - 86

df_sun <- make_embedding(y_sun, p_max = 10)
in_sun  <- df_sun[df_sun$time <= in_end_sun, ]
out_sun <- df_sun[df_sun$time >  in_end_sun, ]
folds_sun <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_sun)))

sun_pw_list <- list()
for (p_order in c(2, 4, 7, 10)) {
  m_sun <- lm(reformulate(paste0("lag_", 1:p_order), response = "target"), data = in_sun)
  t_sun <- rmse(out_sun$target, predict(m_sun, newdata = out_sun))
  
  sun_pw_list[[length(sun_pw_list) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    Order = paste0("AR(", p_order, ")"),
    True_RMSE = round(t_sun, 3),
    Ordinary_CV = round(eval_ord_cv(in_sun, p_order, folds_sun), 3),
    Gap_CV = round(eval_gap_cv(in_sun, p_order, folds_sun, gap = p_order), 3),
    PW_Innov_CV = round(eval_pw_innov_cv(in_sun, p_order, folds_sun), 3),
    PW_Cov_CV = round(eval_pw_cov_cv(in_sun, p_order, folds_sun), 3)
  )
}
sun_pw_df <- do.call(rbind, sun_pw_list)
cat("\n=== Sunspots Pre-whitened CV Comparison ===\n")
print(sun_pw_df)
write.csv(sun_pw_df, file.path(csv_dir, "table_prewhitened_cv_sunspot.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 6. Advanced Extension 2: Joint Selection Criterion (CV Error + Autocorrelation Penalty)

## 6.1 Replacing the Arbitrary Two-Step Filter
In Section 6 of Bergmeir et al. (2018), model selection across the 1560 neural network configurations for the Sunspot series relied on a two-step heuristic:
- **Step 1**: Discard any configuration whose out-of-fold residuals yield a Ljung-Box $p$-value $\le 0.05$.
- **Step 2**: From the surviving models, select the one with minimal CV RMSE.

This hard cutoff has three notable limitations:
1. It is discontinuous: a model with $p = 0.049$ is discarded entirely, while $p = 0.051$ is treated as having zero autocorrelation.
2. It cannot trade off forecast accuracy against marginal degrees of autocorrelation.
3. It does not provide a smooth objective for continuous hyperparameter tuning.

We propose a **Joint Penalized Objective**:
$$\mathcal{J}_\lambda(\theta) = \text{RMSE}_{\text{CV}}(\theta) \times \left(1 + \lambda \cdot \left(1 - p_{\text{LB}}(\theta)\right)\right)$$
where $\lambda \ge 0$ is a tuning penalty parameter. When $\lambda = 0$, the criterion reduces to pure CV error. As $\lambda$ increases, configurations with lingering serial correlation ($p_{\text{LB}} \to 0$) are penalized continuously.

```{r}
## ---------- Extension 2: Joint Selection Criterion on Sunspots ----------
sun_configs <- read.csv(if (file.exists("csv/sunspot_all_configs.csv")) "csv/sunspot_all_configs.csv" else if (file.exists("../csv/sunspot_all_configs.csv")) "../csv/sunspot_all_configs.csv" else file.path(csv_dir, "sunspot_all_configs.csv"))

# Standard 2-step filter baseline (paper's method)
passed_2step <- sun_configs[!is.na(sun_configs$lb_p) & sun_configs$lb_p > 0.05, ]
best_2step <- passed_2step[which.min(passed_2step$cv_rmse), ]

# Evaluate Joint Criterion across penalty grid lambda in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0}
lambda_grid <- c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0)
joint_results <- list()

for (lam in lambda_grid) {
  # Penalized joint score
  scores <- sun_configs$cv_rmse * (1 + lam * (1 - sun_configs$lb_p))
  best_idx <- which.min(scores)
  selected <- sun_configs[best_idx, ]
  
  joint_results[[length(joint_results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    Criterion = if (lam == 0) "Pure CV (lambda=0)" else paste0("Joint Pen (lambda=", lam, ")"),
    Lambda    = lam,
    p_Lags    = selected$p,
    Size      = selected$size,
    Decay     = selected$decay,
    CV_RMSE   = round(selected$cv_rmse, 3),
    LB_p      = round(selected$lb_p, 3),
    Out_RMSE  = round(selected$out_rmse, 3),
    Joint_Score = round(scores[best_idx], 3)
  )
}

table_joint_criterion <- do.call(rbind, joint_results)

# Append the 2-step filter and OOS baseline for immediate comparison
baseline_rows <- data.frame(
  Criterion   = c("Two-Step Filter (Paper)", "OOS Holdout Selection"),
  Lambda      = c(NA, NA),
  p_Lags      = c(best_2step$p, 3),
  Size        = c(best_2step$size, 13),
  Decay       = c(best_2step$decay, 0.05),
  CV_RMSE     = c(round(best_2step$cv_rmse, 3), round(sun_configs[which.min(sun_configs$oos_rmse), "cv_rmse"], 3)),
  LB_p        = c(round(best_2step$lb_p, 3), round(sun_configs[which.min(sun_configs$oos_rmse), "lb_p"], 3)),
  Out_RMSE    = c(round(best_2step$out_rmse, 3), 2.626),
  Joint_Score = c(NA, NA)
)

table_joint_full <- rbind(table_joint_criterion, baseline_rows)

cat("\n=== Joint Selection Criterion vs. Two-Step Filter on Sunspot Grid ===\n")
print(table_joint_full)
write.csv(table_joint_full, file.path(csv_dir, "table_extension_joint_criterion.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```


# 7. Advanced Extension 3: Recursive vs. Direct Multi-Step Cross-Validation ($h \in \{1, 2, 4\}$)

## 7.1 Direct vs. Recursive Forecasting Mechanics
In multi-step time series forecasting, practitioners choose between two core paradigms:
1. **Direct Multi-Step Forecasting**: Train a separate regression model for each horizon $h$:
$$y_{t+h} = g_h(y_t, y_{t-1}, \dots) + \epsilon_{t+h}^{(D)}$$
By construction, adjacent direct forecasts overlap by $h-1$ steps, making $\epsilon_{t+h}^{(D)}$ an $\text{MA}(h-1)$ process.
2. **Recursive Multi-Step Forecasting**: Train a single one-step-ahead model ($h = 1$):
$$y_{t+1} = g_1(y_t, y_{t-1}, \dots) + \epsilon_{t+1}^{(R)}$$
Under correct specification, $\epsilon_{t+1}^{(R)}$ is genuine white noise (Assumption A3 strictly holds!). Predictions for $h > 1$ are generated by feeding previous forecasts recursively into $g_1$.

We investigate whether cross-validating the recursive estimator provides more accurate error estimation (lower MAPAE and bias) than direct cross-validation across horizons $h \in \{1, 2, 4\}$.

```{r}
## ---------- Extension 3: Recursive vs. Direct Multi-Step CV ----------
set.seed(42)

n_trials_rd <- 20

recursive_forecast_step <- function(coefs, history, h, p) {
  curr <- history[1:p]
  preds <- numeric(h)
  for (s in 1:h) {
    y_hat <- coefs[1] + sum(coefs[-1] * curr)
    preds[s] <- y_hat
    curr <- c(y_hat, curr[1:(p - 1)])
  }
  preds[h]
}

cat("Running Recursive vs. Direct Multi-Step CV Monte Carlo Simulation...\n")
rec_dir_list <- list()

for (h in c(1, 2, 4)) {
  for (tr in 1:n_trials_rd) {
    y <- make_series("AR3")
    
    # 1-step dataset for recursive model training
    df_1 <- make_multistep_dataset(y, h = 1, max_lag = 3)
    in_1 <- df_1[df_1$time <= in_end, ]
    
    # h-step dataset for direct forecasting and out-set evaluation
    df_h <- make_multistep_dataset(y, h = h, max_lag = 3)
    in_h  <- df_h[df_h$time <= in_end, ]
    out_h <- df_h[df_h$time > in_end, ]
    
    form_ar3 <- target ~ lag_1 + lag_2 + lag_3
    
    # --- True Out-Set Errors ---
    # Direct model fit on full in_h
    fit_dir_full <- lm(form_ar3, data = in_h)
    true_dir_rmse <- rmse(out_h$target, predict(fit_dir_full, newdata = out_h))
    
    # Recursive model fit on full in_1
    fit_rec_full <- lm(form_ar3, data = in_1)
    c_rec_full <- coef(fit_rec_full)
    rec_out_preds <- sapply(out_h$time, function(tgt_t) {
      orig_t <- tgt_t - h
      hist_vals <- y[orig_t:(orig_t - 3 + 1)]
      recursive_forecast_step(c_rec_full, hist_vals, h, 3)
    })
    true_rec_rmse <- rmse(out_h$target, rec_out_preds)
    
    # --- Cross-Validation ---
    folds_h <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = nrow(in_h)))
    
    # 1. Direct 5-fold CV
    cv_dir_preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_h))
    for (k in 1:n_folds) {
      te <- which(folds_h == k)
      tr <- which(folds_h != k)
      m_dir <- lm(form_ar3, data = in_h[tr, ])
      cv_dir_preds[te] <- predict(m_dir, newdata = in_h[te, ])
    }
    cv_dir_rmse <- rmse(in_h$target, cv_dir_preds)
    
    # 2. Recursive 5-fold CV
    cv_rec_preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(in_h))
    for (k in 1:n_folds) {
      te <- which(folds_h == k)
      te_targets <- in_h$time[te]
      tr_1_idx <- which(!in_1$time %in% te_targets)
      m_rec <- lm(form_ar3, data = in_1[tr_1_idx, ])
      c_rec_k <- coef(m_rec)
      
      for (i in te) {
        orig_t <- in_h$time[i] - h
        hist_vals <- y[orig_t:(orig_t - 3 + 1)]
        cv_rec_preds[i] <- recursive_forecast_step(c_rec_k, hist_vals, h, 3)
      }
    }
    cv_rec_rmse <- rmse(in_h$target, cv_rec_preds)
    
    rec_dir_list[[length(rec_dir_list) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      Horizon       = paste0("h = ", h),
      True_Dir_RMSE = true_dir_rmse,
      CV_Dir_RMSE   = cv_dir_rmse,
      Dir_MAPAE     = abs(cv_dir_rmse - true_dir_rmse),
      Dir_MPAE      = cv_dir_rmse - true_dir_rmse,
      True_Rec_RMSE = true_rec_rmse,
      CV_Rec_RMSE   = cv_rec_rmse,
      Rec_MAPAE     = abs(cv_rec_rmse - true_rec_rmse),
      Rec_MPAE      = cv_rec_rmse - true_rec_rmse
    )
  }
}

rec_dir_df <- do.call(rbind, rec_dir_list)

table_rec_dir <- aggregate(cbind(True_Dir_RMSE, CV_Dir_RMSE, Dir_MAPAE, Dir_MPAE,
                                 True_Rec_RMSE, CV_Rec_RMSE, Rec_MAPAE, Rec_MPAE) ~ Horizon,
                           data = rec_dir_df, FUN = mean)

cat("\n=== Recursive vs. Direct Multi-Step CV Simulation Results ===\n")
print(table_rec_dir)
write.csv(table_rec_dir, file.path(csv_dir, "table_extension_recursive_direct.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## Comparative Visualization for the Extensions
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))

# Plot 1: Pre-whitened vs nonDepCV vs Standard CV MAPAE
barplot(table_prewhitened$MAPAE, names.arg = c("5-Fold", "Gap-CV", "PW-Innov", "PW-Cov", "OOS"),
        col = c("#3b82f6", "#ef4444", "#10b981", "#8b5cf6", "#f59e0b"),
        main = "Misspecified DGP: Estimation Error", ylab = "MAPAE", las = 2)

# Plot 2: Joint Criterion Out-Set RMSE vs Lambda
plot(table_joint_criterion$Lambda, table_joint_criterion$Out_RMSE, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "darkblue",
     xlab = "Penalty Parameter (Lambda)", ylab = "Out-Set RMSE",
     main = "Joint Criterion Out-Set RMSE")
abline(h = best_2step$out_rmse, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright", legend = c("Joint Criterion", "2-Step Filter"), col = c("darkblue", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), pch = c(19, NA))

plot(1:3, table_rec_dir$Dir_MAPAE, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "purple",

     main = "Direct vs. Recursive CV Error")

par(op)
```
